CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. City Region is the City Region of Banjar.
2. City Regional Government is the Mayor as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Banjar.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution that is positioned as an element of Regional Government administration.
5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Mayor and Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government that is the authority of the region.
6. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
7. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, as well as receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Woman is a person who is female by sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman.
9. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb.
10. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence that occurs within the Regional territory.
11. Violence is any act against women and children that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully.
12. Empowerment of women is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and earn independently after being recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
13. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
14. Social rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological and social conditions in order to be able to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
15. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families and communities.
16. Assistance is an activity to provide counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims carried out by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise.
17. Prevention is the effort of the government together with families and communities as well as the private sector and/or business world to prevent the occurrence of violence through socialization, education, advocacy and promotion activities.
18. Handling is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing, and knowing that violence against victims will, is, and/or has occurred.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy, and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is a technical implementing unit of the Regional Apparatus that carries out technical operational activities and/or technical supporting activities for integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
22. Forum for the Protection of Victims of Violence hereinafter abbreviated as FPKK is a coordination forum for prevention, handling and empowerment of victims of violence against women and children whose implementation is carried out in a networked manner and is formed at the Regional, sub-district, and village levels.

CHAPTER VI
OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
OF THE CITY REGIONAL GOVERNMENT
Article 17
(1) The City Regional Government carries out efforts to prevent the occurrence of violence against Women and Children in the form of:
a. collecting data and organizing an information system for the Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence;
b. conducting education on anti-violence values toward Women and Children; and
c. conducting dissemination of laws and regulations related to Women's Empowerment and the Protection of Child Victims of Violence.
(2) The City Regional Government is obliged and responsible to provide and organize services for Victims in the form of:
a. establishing and organizing technical service institutions for Victims by involving elements of the community; and
b. encouraging public awareness of the importance of protection for Victims of violence.

Paragraph 1
Prevention of Violence against Children

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BANJAR CITY
NUMBER 10 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children are experiencing an increasingly rising trend. Economic factors, the social environment and technological development have a major influence on the increase of such acts of violence.
This condition requires the Regional Government to take concrete steps through program activities as efforts to prevent and protect women and children from acts of violence. One of the efforts to prevent violence against women is carried out through women's empowerment and optimization of previously possessed potential, so that it is expected to be able to improve and develop themselves to play a role and be protected from potential acts of violence. This condition will strengthen the form of appreciation and respect for women while maintaining their role and nature as women to play a role in educating and supporting the welfare and happiness of their families. Efforts to prevent violence against children are the obligation of parents, families, communities and the private sector.
Community service is the frontline when potential violence against children occurs. The mechanism for violence prevention efforts and protection of child victims of violence involves multiple sectors coordinated by the Regional Government. The intended efforts are carried out with the direction of providing social rehabilitation for child victims of violence, reintegrating child victims of violence with their families and/or environment, and increasing the empowerment of child victims of violence.
In connection with this matter, to realize the provision of protection efforts for women and children victims of violence as well as for legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection of child victims of violence in the Regional area, it is necessary to regulate it in a Regional Regulation.

Article 12
(1) Prevention of Violence against Children as referred to in Article 11 letter a shall be implemented by:
a. establishing a network in efforts to Prevent Violence against Children;
b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of Violence Prevention based on partnership patterns with the community, private sector and Non-Governmental Organizations; and
c. conducting socialization of laws and regulations related to the Protection of Child Victims of Violence.
(2) Prevention of Violence against Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in an integrated manner and coordinated by the Regional Apparatus responsible for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.

Article 9
Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear.
Paragraph (2) What is meant by "in a networked manner" is that the Regional Government may, through coordination among relevant agencies, undertake efforts to protect child victims of violence and to provide recovery for victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
Paragraph (3) Sufficiently clear.

5.6.rationale: The original Indonesian text explicitly defines “sosialisasi” as dissemination of legal/regulatory information through “media massa, media elektronik, dan/atau penyuluhan langsung kepada masyarakat” (Elucidation of Pasal 7 huruf c). This is a clear, direct reference to using media channels (mass media/electronic media) for outreach/engagement. The retrieved English candidate [5.6-52] accurately reflects this, and the judge’s reasoning (that the policy recognizes media channels in prevention outreach) is consistent with the source text. Therefore the golden label of “No” appears incorrect for a ‘media engagement’ indicator framed around acknowledging/using media for dissemination.

6.7.evaluator_rationale: While the policy states non-discrimination across ethnicity, religion, race, culture, and language, it does not establish special protection measures specifically targeted at women from minority or isolated groups.

6.7.rationale: The original Indonesian regulation does not appear to include any specific provisions targeting women from minority/isolated groups (e.g., indigenous, remote, minority women) with special measures. What it does include is a general non-discrimination principle: protection is provided to every woman/child and “tidak dibedakan berdasarkan suku, agama, ras, golongan, jenis kelamin, etnis, budaya dan bahasa, status hukum, dan kondisi fisik maupun mental” (Penjelasan Pasal 3 huruf b), which is exactly what the retrieved passage [6.7-48] says. If the indicator requires explicit mention of minority groups or tailored measures, the correct answer should be No, making the golden label “Yes” likely wrong (golden_label_issue). Separately, if the evaluation rubric intended that broad non-discrimination across ethnicity/religion/race/culture/language counts as addressing minority women, then the judge was too strict in requiring ‘special measures’ and should have answered Yes based on [6.7-48] (evaluation_failure). The discrepancy likely stems from a mismatch/ambiguity in how the indicator is defined versus how the golden label was applied.
